statement: A ReDoS guard built from fixed adversarial families proves only those shapes. Cejel's regex-redos-guard passed 734 literals, yet adding one family (a key, a 20,000-blank run, then a non-blank) exposed three quadratic regexes on repository text that had shipped through 0.6.7: /\s+#.*$/ twice and /\s*\)+$/u, each retrying a blank run from every position (80,000 characters took 3-4 s). It was found only because a reviewer of PR 540 asked for a quote-and-backslash family. Rules: when adding a regex over untrusted text, add a guard family built from the characters its adjacent quantified classes share (blanks for \s, the class itself for [^x]*), and prefer a linear scan (indexOf, trimEnd) to an unanchored quantified prefix.
